Generation

Explore a diverse collection of shapes by building on promising specimens as the search runs.

How does MAP-Elites work?

Generate batch uses your settings for the first specimen, then samples random parameter combinations. MAP-Elites learns from the specimens it generates: each result can become a parent for later variations in the same search.

The morphology archive groups valid shapes using descriptors selected for each geometry family. Each cell holds one representative—the “elite.” Kept specimens rank first; otherwise, the specimen with the largest connected-solid fraction wins. This score measures connected geometry, not visual appeal.

When the archive has entries for the current recipe family, about 90% of attempts vary an existing elite and 10% explore random parameters. An empty archive starts with random samples.

Candidates sets the number of attempts. Variation scale controls how far offspring move from their parent’s parameters. Results appear as they finish. Keep the ones you like: starting another batch purges unkept specimens.
